description: Synthetic, deterministic. The fixture serves /reports (200) with a 'Download monthly report' link to /reports/monthly.csv; in this scenario's fixture mode the real local server answers that URL with HTTP 503 and a bare HTML 'Service Unavailable' page, without a Content-Disposition attachment. No route, mock or fulfillment is involved. The test waits for a download event and clicks the link, which is a correct way to download the file: in Chromium the 503 HTML response is a navigation, so the browser shows the error page, no download event fires, and the test ends at the 15 s test timeout ('page.waitForEvent: Test timeout of 15000ms exceeded', 'waiting for event "download"', reported at the waitForEvent line 7). The identical spec passed against the healthy mode (200 text/csv attachment) in the isolated Playwright 1.64.1 feasibility run, with the correct filename and contents; there is no formal control, as for S04. The 503 status and the absence of route interception are visible only through get_trace_summary (document GET /reports/monthly.csv, status 503, marker none, no interception patterns or route calls); error-context and the screenshot show the error page text. Application defect is the expected classification: the app fails to serve the report while its pages load. Environment issue is reviewable, because a 503 often means a dependency or the service itself is down; the investigator has no server logs and a single run, so whether the outage is transient stays unknown either way. The timeout is a symptom, not a timing problem.

reviewableAlternatives.note: A 503 Service Unavailable can come from where the service runs (a down dependency, deployment, overload) rather than the application code; defensible only when supported by the observed 503 and cautious about the operational cause, which the artifacts do not show. A 503 alone does not make it an environment issue

requires.description: Supports it with the HTTP 503 / Service Unavailable response to the report download and states that the underlying operational cause is uncertain

rootCause.summary: The test correctly waits for a download and clicks the report link, but the server answers GET /reports/monthly.csv with HTTP 503 and an HTML error page instead of the CSV attachment; Chromium shows that page, no download event fires, and the test times out waiting for it.

criteria.description: Identifies the HTTP 503 / Service Unavailable response
Points at the report download request
Recognizes that the browser showed an error page instead of downloading a file
Recognizes that no download event occurred
Connects the test timeout to waiting for that event
Recognizes that the test's download steps are correct

requiredEvidence.why: Confirmed (Playwright 1.64.1): the top error is 'Test timeout of 15000ms exceeded.' with no location; additionalErrors[0] is 'page.waitForEvent: Test timeout of 15000ms exceeded.' with the log 'waiting for event "download"' at tests/ui/reports.spec.ts:7, cut at 500 characters only after the snippet (the stack line is lost)
The spec waits for a download, clicks the report link and sets up no routing or mocking
Confirmed (Playwright 1.64.1): the page snapshot at failure is the error page, heading "Service Unavailable" and 'The report service is temporarily unavailable.'

Confirmed (Playwright 1.64.1, get_trace_summary): document GET /reports/monthly.csv answered 503 'Service Unavailable' with marker none, before the failure; no interception patterns and no route calls. It is the only source of the HTTP status

acceptable.description: Investigate or repair the report endpoint and its dependencies, restoring the CSV attachment response
Optionally makes the test fail fast by checking the response status before waiting for the download
States the test itself needs no change

forbidden.description: Mocks the download so the test passes
